records.product: Adobe Marketo Engage (connector for AI assistants)
records.assistant: Claude (Claude Desktop and Claude Code only; Claude on the web is not named). ChatGPT is not named: from OpenAI only Codex, a coding tool. Adobe also names Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code with GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Glean.
records.what_adobe_says: Adobe says this is generally available. A Marketo client's team can connect Claude's desktop app or Claude Code to its Marketo instance and, in plain language, look things up and make changes: forms, programs, smart campaigns, emails and snippets, people and lists, and bulk exports. Adobe hosts the service, so the client runs no server. It is a set-up for a technical person, not a one-click install: a Marketo admin creates API credentials in LaunchPoint (Adobe advises a dedicated API-only user with only the permissions needed), and those go into the assistant's settings. For Claude Desktop the person also downloads a small helper file from Adobe and needs Node.js on their computer. What the assistant can do is limited to that API user's permissions and Marketo's usual API limits, and some changes ask for confirmation. Adobe's service only accepts Marketo instances that have been approved for it. With these credentials, SMS, push, in-app message and user management actions are not supported. For the 'ChatGPT' half of Adam's question: Adobe names no ChatGPT set-up for Marketo; OpenAI appears only through Codex. Second reader's notes: (1) the words 'Generally Available' are on Adobe's on-demand event page on Experience League only; the product documentation page and the Marketo release notes page saved here carry no release label and no beta or preview label either, so nothing contradicts it. (2) Two real limits to keep in anything published: Adobe's service 'only accepts requests for approved Marketo instances', and Adobe provides the integration 'as is' and encourages a sandbox test first. (3) This is a Claude-only finding for the tool: it supports a Claude connection to Marketo Engage, not a ChatGPT one.

records.product: Adobe Experience Platform Edge Network (data collection from a client's own ChatGPT app)
records.assistant: ChatGPT only (ChatGPT Apps). Claude is not named.
records.what_adobe_says: Everything the research says about this page is on the page, word for word checked. The verdict changes only because of what kind of thing it is: it is not a connection between ChatGPT and an Adobe product that a client's team switches on. It is a build pattern for a client that has its own app inside ChatGPT (for example a store or office finder that ChatGPT users can call). Adobe shows how that app can send what happens in those conversations to Adobe as analytics data, and get personalization decisions back to show in the app's panel inside ChatGPT. The client builds and owns the app's back end; Adobe calls the page 'a reference implementation intended to illustrate an integration pattern' and tells the client to review security, privacy and consent before using it. No beta or preview label anywhere on the page. Claude is not named. For the tool: Edge Network is not a product on the canvas and Adobe's page names no receiving product (not Customer Journey Analytics, Adobe Analytics, Target, Journey Optimizer or Real-Time CDP), so there is no card pair to draw a connection between. If it is used at all, it fits as optional partner build work (a service), not as a ChatGPT connection.
